summary: In a major civil and commercial space development, NASA has awarded Blue Origin a $700 million contract to build a new Mars orbiter and serve as a Martian telecommunications network provider. In international launch and commercial operations, China’s private, reusable Pallas-1 rocket successfully completed its debut flight, Astroscale selected Isar to launch a space debris removal mission, and York Space Systems unveiled a new Very Low Earth Orbit satellite platform. In government policy and military space developments, the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy advised U.S. space companies to skip an upcoming French space summit, President Trump ordered a study to establish a U.S. Space Academy, and the Pentagon issued contracts to boost space systems manufacturing capacity as Congress passed a short-term funding bill. Meanwhile, NASA mounted historic engines onto hardware for the planned Artemis III mission. In scientific discoveries, NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope tracked a newly observed 10-sided decagon cloud structure at Saturn’s south pole, while data from the final atmospheric reentry of the Cluster mission and a NASA sounding rocket flight provided new insights into satellite design safety and radio-disrupting clouds. Readers should watch on September 3 as two joint European and Japanese spacecraft begin their long-awaited arrival at Mercury.
